$comment: The postbuild check used to print one figure, `largest bundle 927 files`,
and every standing report read it as a bundle size. It is not a size and it
is not a bundle: it is the CARDINALITY of a Next server trace manifest — how
many files the server bundle traces — and it says nothing at all about the
JavaScript a reader downloads. The two questions were being answered by one
ambiguous number, so neither was being answered.
They are separate budgets now, both printed by the postbuild check, and both
numbers appear in standing reports from here on in place of the old figure.
ON MAPLIBRE. It is reported separately because 75% of the reader's initial
JavaScript is the map library, and a total that hides that tells nobody
anything actionable. It is NOT excluded from the total, and it must not be:
the author's instruction is explicit — the map IS the landing product, and a
budget gamed by moving the biggest thing out of scope measures nothing.
$ceilingRule: THE CEILING RULE, ONE RULE, STATED HERE AND ENFORCED IN THE SUITE
Until now every ceiling in this file was a number with a paragraph of
justification and no rule behind it — 23% here, 14% there, 8% somewhere
else. Headroom by choice is indistinguishable from headroom bought to turn
a red check green, which is the one thing the author's standing order
forbids. So:
A ceiling is AT MOST the measured baseline plus 15%, rounded DOWN to a
readable unit — 10 for file counts, 10,000 for byte figures.
Rounding down, always, so rounding can never buy headroom the rule did not
grant. It is a CAP, not a formula: a ceiling TIGHTER than the cap is always
allowed and needs no reason, and a ceiling already committed is never raised
toward the cap just because the cap allows it.
A ceiling therefore moves for exactly one reason: a re-measured baseline
moved under it, committed with what changed recorded as its reason. The
headroom is not where a real change gets absorbed — it is only there so an
ordinary dependency bump does not fail a build and teach people to raise
ceilings.
`scripts/check-build-output.mjs` exports HEADROOM and ceilingCap();
`tests/build-budget.test.ts` holds every ceiling below to them.
WHAT THE RULE CHANGED WHEN IT WAS ADOPTED, stated rather than left to a
diff: serverTrace.appManifest.ceiling came DOWN from 240 to 220, because 240
was above the cap for a baseline of 195. The framework ceilings and the
client ceilings were already at or below their caps and did not move — 1300
is exactly the cap for 1138, which is the derivation it was missing.
$serverTraceComment: SPLIT INTO TWO NUMBERS AND MEASURED PER MODE (R51 remainder, 2026-08-18, g16).
The single figure below used to be `Math.max` over every manifest, which is
always next-server.js — the FRAMEWORK's own runtime trace, holding zero files
of ours. It refused a deploy for a reason unrelated to what it guards, and it
could have passed for the exact defect it exists to catch: under one maximum,
an app route could grow 195 -> 900 files and stay far under a ceiling pinned
to the framework's 927.
THE MEASUREMENTS THAT SETTLED IT, all four taken 2026-08-18:
927  windows, default mode      (what the old baseline was)
935  linux,   default mode      (+8: @img/sharp-linux* for sharp-win32)
1130  windows, standalone mode   (+203, all of them node_modules/next/dist)
1138  linux,   standalone mode   (what Netlify built, and refused)
Netlify's Next runtime plugin builds in STANDALONE mode, so 1138 is the only
one of the four that describes a deploy. The old baseline was the only one of
the four that described nothing that ships.
THE 203 FILES THAT JOINED IN STANDALONE MODE, recorded as this ceiling's
reason rather than summarised: every one is under node_modules/next/dist and
none is a file of this repo's — dist/lib/metadata (20), dist/lib/typescript
(11), dist/compiled/@edge-runtime (11), dist/shared/lib (9), dist/lib/helpers
(8), dist/build/swc (7), dist/telemetry/events (5), dist/trace/report (4),
dist/lib/memory (4), dist/build/segment-config (3), and singles and pairs
across dist/build, dist/compiled and dist/lib. Standalone mode exists to make
the server runnable without node_modules, so tracing its own runtime is the
mode working. Zero app-route manifests changed between the two modes: every
one is byte-identical, which is what makes 1a mode-independent.
Reproduce any of it with `node scripts/trace-census.mjs --files out.txt` and
diff two builds' dumps; .github/workflows/build-check.yml runs both modes on
linux so the deployed number is measured before Netlify measures it.

appManifest.what: Files traced into the largest manifest under .next/server/app — the routes that carry OUR code. A COUNT, not bytes. This is the number R23 blew up to 2554 and 2567 when a runtime-computed path made Turbopack trace the whole project, tests/ included.
appManifest.ceilingNote: The cap for a baseline of 195: floor(195 * 1.15 / 10) * 10. It was 240 until 2026-08-18 (g17), justified by /api/meetings legitimately tracing public/geo/** through outputFileTracingIncludes — real, but it is a reason for the BASELINE to move when a state is onboarded, not a reason for the ceiling to sit above the rule. Onboarding a state now re-measures 195 and records the boundary files that joined, which is the record that was previously being skipped.
appManifest.modeIndependent: Measured identical in default and standalone mode on 2026-08-18. If these ever diverge, the divergence is the finding.

frameworkRuntime.what: Files traced into next-server.js — Next's own server runtime. Contains no file of this repo. Recorded per BUILD MODE because the mode changes it by 200+ files, and compared against the mode actually built, never across modes.

standalone.modeNote: The mode Netlify builds in: its Next runtime plugin sets NEXT_PRIVATE_STANDALONE. Measured on linux, the platform Netlify builds on.
standalone.ceilingNote: Exactly the cap for a baseline of 1138: floor(1138 * 1.15 / 10) * 10 = 1300. This number was previously committed with no derivation at all, which is what AUD-02 1b sent g17 to fix; the number itself turned out to be the one the rule produces, so it did not move.

default.modeNote: A plain `pnpm build` with no standalone output — what a developer runs locally. Measured on linux; windows reads 927, and the 8-file gap is @img/sharp-linux* standing in for @img/sharp-win32-x64.
default.ceilingNote: TIGHTER than the cap, which is 1070. A tighter ceiling is always allowed and needs no reason; this one has never refused a build and is left where it is rather than raised toward the cap, because the rule caps headroom and never manufactures it.

$clientComment: BUDGET 2, RE-BASELINED ON THE BUILD THAT DEPLOYS (g17, 2026-08-18).
The figures here were first committed on 2026-08-18 (g16) from a WINDOWS
build in DEFAULT mode. That is the same class of mistake the framework
baseline made when it was pinned at 927: a real measurement of a build
nobody ships. They are re-taken here from the ubuntu standalone job of
.github/workflows/build-check.yml — the same command, the same runner class
and the same mode as the Netlify deploy — and the run is named below so the
number can be re-read rather than trusted.
WHAT MOVED, and it is small enough to be worth naming precisely: raw
is the PLATFORM, not the mode — the ubuntu standalone job and the ubuntu
default job printed identical client figures to the byte, and only the
windows build differed. Client cost is therefore mode-independent in the
same way budget 1a is, and platform-dependent in a way budget 1a is not.
HOW IT IS MEASURED. Off the emitted HTML of the prerendered `/`: every
<script src> it names, read from .next/static, raw bytes and gzip -9. That
is what is served rather than what a manifest planned to serve. The wire
figure a real reader gets depends on the CDN's encoding — Netlify may serve
brotli, which is smaller — so gzip -9 is a consistent upper-bound comparison
rather than a claim about one reader's download.
AN UNMEASURED BUDGET 2 REFUSES. If `/` stops being prerendered, or names no
scripts, the check fails rather than printing a zero. A budget that reads a
missing file as 0 bytes passes loudest exactly when it has stopped working.

client.what: The scripts the prerendered / actually references — the reader's initial JavaScript on the landing page. Read from the emitted HTML rather than from a manifest, so it is what is served rather than what was planned.
client.measuredOn: ubuntu-latest, standalone mode — the platform and build mode Netlify deploys. GitHub Actions run 32201893815, job 95917264172 (build-check.yml), 2026-08-18.
client.initialJsCeilingNote: TIGHTER than the cap, which is 3290000 (floor(2861740 * 1.15 / 10000) * 10000). Committed at 3100000 before the rule existed and left there: the rule caps headroom and never manufactures it, so an already-tighter ceiling stays.
client.transferCeilingNote: TIGHTER than the cap, which is 990000. Same reasoning as the raw ceiling. This is the figure closest to what a reader waits for, and it is the one worth keeping tight.
client.split: MapLibre is 75% of the raw initial JS and 75% of the transfer. Tracked apart so a change in application code is visible against it, never to lower the total.
